facts.fact: General Agent is described by Replit as the most flexible way to work with Replit Agent, and users do not need to pre-select an artifact type before chatting.
facts.quote: General Agent is the most flexible way to work with Replit Agent. You don’t need to pre-select an artifact type or commit to building something specific.

facts.fact: Users can access General Agent by selecting "General" before writing a prompt on the Replit home page.
facts.quote: Select “General” before writing a prompt on the Replit home page

facts.fact: Projects imported from GitHub automatically get General Agent, according to Replit's documentation.
facts.quote: Projects imported from GitHub automatically get General Agent

facts.fact: Replit's documentation lists BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, and Hex as currently supported General Agent connectors, plus "and more."
facts.quote: Currently supported: BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, Hex, and more.

facts.fact: According to Replit's documentation, connectors are optional and General Agent can be used for knowledge work, file generation, and app building without external connections.
facts.quote: Connectors are optional. You can use General Agent for knowledge work, file generation, and building apps without any external connections.

facts.fact: According to Replit's documentation, each General Agent chat is contained within a single project, and projects cannot communicate with each other.
facts.quote: Each chat is contained within a single project. You can’t have Project A and Project B talk to each other.

facts.fact: Replit's documentation states that agent-based work requires connecting services through Connectors, because Agent does not have access to external tools by default.
facts.quote: You need to connect your services first through Connectors. Once connected, Agent can read and write to them, but it doesn’t have access by default.

facts.fact: Replit's documentation warns that some technologies may not be fully supported in the Nix environment used by General Agent.
facts.quote: Some technologies may not be fully supported in the Nix environment

facts.fact: According to Replit's documentation, General Agent sets up its own environment and runs commands based on the request, unlike standard Agent with pre-configured environments.
facts.quote: Unlike standard Agent with pre-configured environments, General Agent sets up its own environment and run commands based on your request.

facts.fact: Replit's documentation says users may need to ask General Agent to configure publishing when they are ready to deploy.
facts.quote: You may need to ask it to configure publishing when you’re ready to deploy.
